summary: This week’s launch is blocked by unresolved handling of sensitive patient data, clinical-safety validation, SMS delivery safeguards, and the absence of named accountability.

concerns.concern: Name an accountable security, privacy, and legal decision owner before launch.
evidence: No security/privacy/legal owner is named.
unknowns: Who can make and document security, privacy, and legal decisions for launch.
concerns.rationale: There is no identified authority to accept or resolve risks involving patient information and clinical recommendations.

concerns.concern: Decide whether privacy review is required before launch rather than accepting an unspecified post-launch review.
evidence: The founder says to skip privacy review until after launch.
The product stores symptoms and insurance identifiers.
unknowns: Whether any authorized owner accepts the consequences of deferring review.
What privacy requirements apply to the intended deployment.
concerns.rationale: Deferring review can leave material data-handling obligations unidentified at launch.

concerns.concern: Determine the applicable privacy, security, and healthcare-regulatory constraints for the intended hospital-patient workflow.
evidence: The intake is for US hospital patients.
The system stores symptoms and insurance identifiers.
unknowns: Whether participating hospitals or the service are subject to particular healthcare privacy or security requirements.
The role of the founder's organization relative to each hospital.
The applicable jurisdictions and contractual terms.
concerns.rationale: Applicable external requirements can determine whether the proposed collection, storage, vendors, and messaging are permissible.

concerns.concern: Define the minimum necessary collection, storage, access, retention, and deletion approach for symptoms, insurance identifiers, and debugging data.
evidence: The system stores symptoms and insurance identifiers.
Raw prompts are retained for debugging.
unknowns: Which fields are necessary for the service.
Who may access stored data.
How long each category of data would be retained.
Whether raw prompts contain patient information.
concerns.rationale: The chosen data lifecycle directly affects exposure of sensitive patient information and the implementation scope.

concerns.concern: Establish whether and how patient data may be sent to the LLM, including the provider's data use, retention, and security terms.
evidence: An LLM recommends urgency.
Raw prompts are retained for debugging.
The system stores symptoms and insurance identifiers.
unknowns: Which LLM provider will be used.
What patient data is included in prompts.
Whether the provider retains or uses submitted prompts.
Whether required agreements or controls are available.
concerns.rationale: LLM integration may transmit sensitive patient information to a third party and can constrain the product design.

concerns.concern: Define intended use, escalation behavior, human involvement, and safety validation for LLM-generated urgency recommendations.
evidence: An LLM recommends urgency.
The intake is for US hospital patients.
unknowns: Whether recommendations are advisory or used to direct patient care.
Who reviews recommendations.
What outcomes count as unsafe.
What test cases, acceptance thresholds, and escalation paths are required.
concerns.rationale: An incorrect urgency recommendation can affect patient safety and determines whether a pilot is safe to conduct.

concerns.concern: Decide the SMS content, consent basis, recipient verification, and handling for failed or misdirected messages.
evidence: SMS sends results.
The system stores symptoms and insurance identifiers.
unknowns: What result content will be sent by SMS.
How patient phone numbers and consent are obtained.
How identity and phone ownership are verified.
What happens if delivery fails or reaches the wrong person.
concerns.rationale: SMS can disclose health-related results to an unintended recipient and may be unreliable for urgent communications.

concerns.concern: Justify, limit, or remove retention of raw prompts for debugging.
evidence: Raw prompts are retained for debugging.
An LLM recommends urgency.
unknowns: Whether prompts contain symptoms, insurance identifiers, or other patient information.
The debugging need, retention duration, and access controls.
concerns.rationale: Raw prompts can create an additional sensitive-data store whose risk may exceed its debugging value.

concerns.concern: Define the minimum evidence required to approve a launch this week, including privacy, data handling, LLM safety, and SMS checks.
evidence: A founder asks to ship this week.
unknowns: Who approves release.
What evidence is sufficient for launch.
Whether a limited pilot is possible before broader release.
concerns.rationale: A time-bound launch request does not establish that material risks have been evaluated or accepted.

concerns.concern: Define how urgency recommendations, message failures, and data-handling issues will be detected and responded to after launch.
evidence: An LLM recommends urgency.
SMS sends results.
Raw prompts are retained for debugging.
unknowns: Who receives and handles incidents.
What signals are available for incorrect recommendations, SMS failures, or inappropriate data access.
Whether service support is available after launch.
concerns.rationale: The workflow has patient-impacting recommendations and sensitive data, so unresolved failures need an operational response path.

questions.question: Which person is authorized to own security, privacy, legal, clinical-safety, and release decisions?
Which hospitals will participate, and what is the organization's role in relation to them?
What exact patient and insurance fields are collected, and which are included in LLM prompts?
Which LLM provider will process the prompts, and what are its retention and data-use terms?
Is the urgency output advisory, who reviews it, and what happens for potentially urgent cases?
What result text will be sent by SMS, how is consent obtained, and how are wrong or failed deliveries handled?
Why are raw prompts needed for debugging, and what retention period and access model are intended?
Can launch begin as a limited pilot, and who sets the evidence required to proceed beyond it?

unsupported_inferences_to_avoid: That the organization is a HIPAA covered entity or business associate.
That HIPAA or any particular law definitively applies.
That the LLM provider retains, trains on, or otherwise uses prompts.
That patients have consented to SMS communication.
That SMS messages will contain insurance identifiers or full clinical details.
That the LLM is intended to diagnose, triage independently, or replace clinician judgment.
That a particular security control, certification, contract, or approval is legally required.
